sections.text: World Arthritis Day reminds us that arthritis is not a single disease — it includes osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, ankylosing spondylitis, lupus-related joint disease, and many other conditions. In Nepal, joint pain is often dismissed as a normal part of ageing. Informed choices about when to seek care, how to use medicines safely, and how to protect joints every day can significantly improve long-term outcomes.
Why early diagnosis matters

Inflammatory arthritis, especially rheumatoid arthritis, causes the most joint damage in the first months to years of disease. Starting disease-modifying treatment early helps preserve function, reduce pain, and lower the risk of disability. A rheumatologist can distinguish inflammatory arthritis from mechanical wear-and-tear and order the right blood tests and imaging.

items: Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
Swelling in multiple joints, especially hands and feet
Symptoms that improve with activity but worsen with rest
Unexplained fatigue alongside joint pain

sections.text: Building better daily habits

Medication is only one part of care. Weight management, joint-friendly exercise, adequate sleep, and smoking cessation all support treatment response. Patients at RAC Nepal receive education on pacing activities, protecting painful joints during household and farm work, and knowing when a flare needs medical review rather than simply waiting it out.
If joint pain is limiting your work, sleep, or independence, specialist evaluation is worthwhile — even if symptoms have been present for years.
Working with your care team

Better outcomes come from partnership: attending follow-up visits, reporting side effects honestly, and asking questions about goals of treatment. World Arthritis Day is an opportunity to replace fear and misinformation with a clear plan — one that fits your life in Nepal and keeps you as active as possible for as long as possible.

Kathmandu has seen growing demand for specialist rheumatology care as awareness of autoimmune and inflammatory joint disease increases across Nepal. At the Rheumatology and Arthritis Center (RAC Nepal), patients receive board-certified rheumatology expertise combined with physiotherapy, pharmacy support, and coordinated follow-up under one roof.
What rheumatologists treat

Rheumatologists diagnose and manage conditions where the immune system or metabolic factors affect joints, muscles, and connective tissue. This includes rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, gout, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, vasculitis, osteoporosis, and complex regional pain syndromes. General physicians and orthopaedic surgeons often refer patients when symptoms suggest inflammation rather than injury alone.

items: Comprehensive history and joint examination
Laboratory and imaging interpretation
Long-term medication monitoring
Flare management and treatment adjustment
Coordination with physiotherapy and rehabilitation

sections.text: The RAC Nepal approach

Our team focuses on precise diagnosis first. Many patients arrive after months of painkillers without a clear label for their condition. We explain findings in plain language, discuss evidence-based options, and respect cultural and financial realities common in Nepal — including the role of family caregivers in treatment decisions.
Established in 2004, RAC Nepal has supported thousands of patients with arthritis and autoimmune disease across Kathmandu and beyond.

Whether you need a first opinion or ongoing specialist supervision, expert arthritis care in Kathmandu should feel accessible, respectful, and practical — not overwhelming. That is the standard we aim for at every consultation.

Knee pain is one of the most common reasons patients visit RAC Nepal. Causes range from osteoarthritis and meniscal injury to inflammatory arthritis, gout, and bursitis. Effective relief starts with the right diagnosis — not every painful knee needs surgery, and not every knee improves with rest alone.
Common causes in Nepal

items: Osteoarthritis from age, weight, or prior injury
Rheumatoid or other inflammatory arthritis
Gout affecting the knee, especially in men
Ligament or meniscus injury after sports or falls
Overuse from stairs, squatting, or farm work

sections.text: Practical relief strategies

Short-term rest during acute flares can help, but prolonged inactivity weakens supporting muscles and worsens stiffness. Low-impact strengthening — straight-leg raises, sit-to-stand practice, and guided physiotherapy — often provides more durable benefit than repeated injections alone. Weight loss, when appropriate, reduces load across the joint with every step.

Footwear matters on Kathmandu’s uneven pavements. Patients who climb many stairs daily benefit from pacing, using handrails, and alternating demanding tasks. Cold packs can calm acute swelling; warmth may ease morning stiffness in osteoarthritis.
Seek specialist care if the knee is hot, markedly swollen, locked, or unable to bear weight — or if pain persists beyond a few weeks despite sensible self-care.
When treatment goes further

Rheumatologists may recommend anti-inflammatory medicines, disease-modifying drugs for inflammatory arthritis, joint injections, or referral for surgical opinion when structural damage is advanced. The goal is stable, confident movement — whether that means returning to temple visits, office work, or family responsibilities without constant fear of the next painful step.

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease that attacks the lining of joints and can affect other organs. Without treatment, it leads to deformity, disability, and reduced life expectancy. Modern rheumatology offers highly effective therapies — but outcomes depend on early referral and consistent follow-up.
How RA is diagnosed

Diagnosis combines symptom pattern, physical examination, blood tests such as rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies, inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), and sometimes ultrasound or X-ray. Symmetric small-joint swelling, prolonged morning stiffness, and elevated inflammation support the diagnosis. Waiting until joints are permanently damaged makes treatment harder.
Treatment options available in Nepal

items: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) such as methotrexate
Short-term corticosteroids during flares
Biologic therapies when conventional DMARDs are insufficient
Pain management and physiotherapy for function
Regular monitoring for medication safety

sections.text: The aim of RA treatment is remission or low disease activity — not merely coping with pain.
Living well with RA

Patients should attend scheduled blood tests, report infections promptly, and avoid stopping medicines without medical advice. Vaccinations, dental care, and bone health assessment are part of long-term planning. At RAC Nepal, we tailor regimens to each patient’s disease severity, comorbidities, and daily responsibilities — because successful RA care is a marathon, not a one-time prescription.

गठिया वा बात रोगले दैनिक कामकाज, निद्रा र मानसिक शान्तिमा प्रभाव पार्छ। नेपालमा धेरै बिरामीले यसलाई उमेर बढेपछि स्वाभाविक ठान्छन्, तर सूजन, बिहानको कडा हुनु र थकान लामो समयसम्म रहँदा विशेषज्ञ जाँच आवश्यक हुन्छ।
दैनिक जीवनमा सजिलो बनाउने उपाय

items: बिहानको कडापन घटाउन हल्का तातो पानी वा गर्म पानीको थैलो प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्
एकै पटक धेरै काम नगरी आरामदायी अन्तराल राख्नुहोस्

sections.text: खाना र जीवनशैली

सन्तुलित खाना, पर्याप्त पानी, र धूम्रपान छोड्नुले सूजन नियन्त्रणमा सहयोग गर्छ। यकृतमा असर पार्ने मादक पदार्थ सीमित राख्नुहोस्। घरको काम, खेतबारी वा पसलको काम गर्दा घुँडा र कम्मरको स्थिति सच्याउनुहोस् — लामो समयसम्म झुकेर काम गर्दा दुखाइ बढ्न सक्छ।
यदि जोर्नी सुन्निन्छ, तातो महसुस हुन्छ वा औषधि लिए पनि दुखाइ बढ्दै जान्छ भने रुम्याटोलोजिस्टसँग भेट्नुहोस्।
विशेषज्ञ सहयोग किन जरुरी

RAC Nepal मा हामी गठिया, रुम्याटोइड अर्थराइटिस, गाउट, लुपस जस्ता विभिन्न बात रोगको अलग–अलग उपचार योजना बनाउँछौं। सही निदान बिना केवल दुखाइको औषधि मात्र लिँदा लामो समयमा जोर्नीमा क्षति हुन सक्छ। समयमै उपचार र नियमित फलो–अपले अधिक आरामपूर्ण जीवन सम्भव बनाउँछ।

Gout is caused by uric acid crystals depositing in joints, often the big toe, ankle, or knee. Flares are intensely painful and can last days to weeks. In Nepal, festivals, social drinking, rich meals, and dehydration are common triggers — understanding them helps prevent recurrence.
Diet and drinks that raise risk

items: Red meat, organ meats, and certain seafood
Excess alcohol, especially beer and spirits
Sweetened beverages and high-fructose foods
Large portions of lentils and some pulses during acute flares
Dehydration in hot weather or after illness

sections.text: Prevention strategies that work

Drink adequate water throughout the day. Maintain a healthy weight gradually — crash dieting can paradoxically trigger flares. Limit alcohol during celebrations and alternate alcoholic drinks with water. If you have had more than one attack, discuss long-term urate-lowering therapy with a rheumatologist — intermittent painkillers alone do not prevent joint damage.
A single gout attack is a warning sign. Repeated flares can lead to chronic arthritis and kidney stones.
When to seek care urgently

Hot, red, exquisitely painful joints need prompt evaluation to rule out infection. RAC Nepal provides uric acid monitoring, flare treatment plans, and education tailored to Nepali dietary patterns — so patients can enjoy cultural meals with sensible limits and protect their joints for the long term.

Osteoporosis weakens bones and increases fracture risk — often silently until a fall causes a wrist, hip, or spine injury. After age 50, especially in postmenopausal women and men with low body weight or steroid use, screening becomes essential. In Nepal, vitamin D deficiency and limited awareness contribute to underdiagnosis.
Who should be screened

items: Women aged 65 and older, or younger with risk factors
Men aged 70 and older
Anyone with prior low-trauma fracture
Long-term steroid users
Patients with rheumatoid arthritis or untreated hyperthyroidism

sections.text: Protecting bone health

Adequate calcium from food or supplements, vitamin D as advised by your doctor, weight-bearing exercise, and fall prevention at home (good lighting, railings, non-slip footwear) all matter. Smoking and heavy alcohol harm bone density. Rheumatologists at RAC Nepal interpret DEXA scans and prescribe bisphosphonates or other therapies when indicated.
A fracture from standing-height or less is often the first sign of osteoporosis — do not wait for back pain alone.
Bone health is part of comprehensive rheumatology care. Treating osteoporosis early preserves independence and reduces the heavy personal and family burden of hip fracture recovery.

Systemic lupus erythematosus (lupus) is an autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints, kidneys, blood cells, and other organs. Symptoms vary widely and mimic other illnesses, which delays diagnosis. Recognising early patterns helps patients in Kathmandu access specialist care sooner.
Possible early signs

items: Butterfly-shaped rash across the cheeks after sun exposure
Joint pain and swelling in multiple areas
Persistent fatigue not explained by sleep or workload
Mouth ulcers, hair loss, or Raynaud’s phenomenon
Unexplained fever, anemia, or kidney problems

sections.text: Why rheumatology referral matters

Lupus requires specific blood tests — including ANA and further autoantibodies — interpreted in clinical context. A positive ANA alone does not confirm lupus. Rheumatologists coordinate treatment with hydroxychloroquine, immunosuppressants, and sun protection, while monitoring kidneys and blood counts over time.
Lupus is manageable with modern therapy. The goal is control of disease activity and prevention of organ damage.

At RAC Nepal, we support patients through flares, pregnancy planning questions, and medication safety — with clear communication for families who often play a central role in care decisions across Nepal.

Patients with arthritis often fear that exercise will damage joints further. In fact, appropriate movement reduces stiffness, strengthens supporting muscles, and improves balance. The key is choosing the right type, intensity, and timing — especially during flares.
Exercises generally safe for arthritic joints

items: Range-of-motion movements for fingers, wrists, and shoulders
Straight-leg raises and seated marching for knee support
Water-based exercise where available
Tai chi or gentle balance work for fall prevention
Posture correction and core stability for back pain

sections.text: What to avoid during flares

High-impact jumping, deep squats on painful knees, and pushing through sharp pain can worsen inflammation. During acute flares, shorten sessions, favour isometric holds, and resume progressive loading as swelling settles. Physiotherapists at RAC Nepal design home programs suited to Nepali living spaces and daily tasks.
Pain rated mild during exercise that settles within an hour is usually acceptable. Sharp or lingering pain is a signal to modify the program.
Combining physiotherapy with medical treatment gives better function than medication alone. Consistency matters more than intensity — ten minutes daily often beats one long session per week.

Many people delay seeing a rheumatologist because they assume joint pain is normal or will resolve with painkillers. Certain warning signs suggest inflammatory or systemic disease that benefits from early specialist assessment.
Seven signs to take seriously

items: Morning stiffness lasting more than 30–60 minutes
Visible swelling in one or more joints
Symptoms in the same joints on both sides of the body
Unexplained skin rash with joint pain or sun sensitivity
Fever, weight loss, or profound fatigue with joint symptoms
Joint pain starting in your 20s or 30s with back stiffness
Poor response to rest and over-the-counter pain relief over weeks

sections.text: What to expect at your visit

Bring previous test results and a list of medicines, including supplements. The rheumatologist will examine all relevant joints, review labs and imaging, and explain whether you need observation, further testing, or treatment. Referral from another doctor is helpful but not always required.
Earlier specialist care for inflammatory arthritis can change the trajectory of disease — waiting for deformity is unnecessary with modern treatment.
If you recognise several of these signs, book a rheumatology consultation at RAC Nepal. Clarifying the diagnosis is the first step toward a plan that protects your joints and your quality of life.

Travel to Kathmandu is difficult for many patients across Nepal — especially for elderly individuals, those in post-flare recovery, or families balancing work and caregiving. Telehealth rheumatology follow-up brings specialist input to your home when an in-person examination is not essential.
What telehealth can cover well

items: Follow-up after an established diagnosis
Medication review and prescription adjustment
Discussion of blood test results
Education on flares, injections, and lifestyle
Planning when in-person assessment is needed

sections.text: When in-person care is still needed

New unexplained swelling, possible joint infection, significant new weakness, or first-time evaluation for complex symptoms usually require physical examination and sometimes ultrasound or aspiration. Telehealth complements — but does not replace — hands-on rheumatology when the clinical situation demands it.
RAC Nepal telehealth is designed for safe continuity of care, not anonymous one-off advice without records.

Patients outside the valley can stay connected to their rheumatologist, reduce unnecessary travel costs, and receive timely adjustments during disease flares. Ask our team whether your next visit can be virtual or should be in clinic.

Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a form of inflammatory arthritis that predominantly affects the spine and sacroiliac joints. It often begins before age 40 — sometimes in the late teens or twenties — and is frequently mislabelled as poor posture, desk work strain, or ‘normal’ back pain.
Clues that suggest AS rather than mechanical pain

items: Back pain and stiffness worse in the morning or after rest
Improvement with exercise, worsening with prolonged sitting
Onset before age 40 with gradual progression over months
Alternating buttock pain or heel pain (Achilles enthesitis)
Family history of AS, psoriasis, or inflammatory bowel disease

sections.text: Diagnosis and treatment

Evaluation includes history, physical examination, inflammatory markers, HLA-B27 testing where appropriate, and MRI of sacroiliac joints when standard X-rays are normal early in disease. NSAIDs, physiotherapy emphasizing spinal mobility, and biologic therapies for persistent inflammation can prevent fusion and preserve function.
Young adults should not accept years of untreated inflammatory back pain as inevitable.

RAC Nepal rheumatologists help distinguish AS from mechanical causes and build long-term plans that keep young professionals, students, and parents active — without unnecessary delay or repeated ineffective painkiller cycles.

Many arthritis patients report worse stiffness when temperatures fall — common in Kathmandu’s winter and in hill regions. Cold does not cause arthritis, but it can increase muscle tightness, reduce circulation, and make existing inflammation feel more pronounced.
Simple winter strategies

items: Dress in layers and keep knees and hands warm outdoors
Do five to ten minutes of gentle mobility before leaving bed
Time medications so peak effect covers morning stiffness when possible
Stay active indoors — avoid sitting in one position for hours
Use warm (not scalding) compresses on stiff joints

sections.text: Hydration and indoor air

People drink less water in cold weather, which can affect overall wellbeing. Heated rooms may dry the air — staying hydrated and ventilating when safe helps. Maintain regular follow-up; winter flares sometimes need temporary treatment adjustment rather than simply enduring until spring.
New severe swelling, redness, or fever with joint pain should be evaluated promptly — not attributed to weather alone.

With planning, winter need not mean months of lost activity. RAC Nepal teams can help you adjust exercise, medications, and home routines so cold weather supports — rather than derails — your joint health goals.
